channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Optimising exercise prescription for cancer-related fatigue, lean mass, physical function and muscle strength in women with breast cancer: a systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and dose-response network meta-analysis (64 trials, n=5156) found that combined exercise was most effective for improving cancer-related fatigue and lean mass, while resistance exercise was most effective for physical function and muscle strength in women with breast cancer, with significant benefits achievable at doses as low as 10–40 min/week.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of supervised exercise during pregnancy on gestational diabetes mellitus and other pregnancy outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis (19 studies, n=6213) found that supervised exercise during pregnancy significantly reduced the risk of gestational diabetes (RR 0.74), gestational hypertension (RR 0.55), excessive gestational weight gain (RR 0.75), and macrosomia (RR 0.61), with greater effects from earlier intervention, higher adherence, combined aerobic and resistance training, and ≥150 min/week exercise.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low to moderate exercise doses were associated with short-term, potentially clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for chronic low back pain, with optimal model-predicted doses of 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control. Exercise-plus interventions (exercise combined with other lifestyle interventions) were significantly better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed, but not for memory.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Fatigue-related neuromuscular outcomes following ACL reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies (n=477) found that individuals post-ACL reconstruction showed greater post-fatigue impairments in quadriceps central activation ratio (SMD: -0.69, p < 0.001) and muscle activation patterns (SMD: -0.62, p < 0.001) compared to healthy controls, with moderate-certainty evidence.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of TENS, NMES, and Combination Therapy on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain and Function After Stroke.
item.description: This prospective randomized study (n=60) found that combined TENS and NMES significantly reduced hemiplegic shoulder pain and improved SPADI scores more than TENS alone, and also improved shoulder ROM, in acute and subacute stroke patients, when added to a standardized rehabilitation program.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) among people with stroke. Balance training and programs integrating cognitive components were most effective, particularly for those in the chronic stage with mild to moderate disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: This sham-controlled RCT (n=85) found that adding 4 weeks of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy to physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (-0.56 MAS points), walking performance (-1.41s 10MWT), functional mobility, motor function, and quality of life in chronic stroke patients with plantar flexor spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Video-based education is non-inferior to in-person education in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial | Archives of Physiotherapy
item.description: A non-inferiority RCT (n=166) found that preoperative video-based education was non-inferior to postoperative in-person education for pain-related self-efficacy (PSEQ MD: -0.6 at T1; -0.5 at T2) and led to better fear of movement scores (TSK) in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
item.author: Arch Physiother

item.title: Physical Therapy Management of Fall Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Adults (CPG+)
item.description: APTA Geriatrics has published an updated Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG+) for the physical therapy management of fall risk in community-dwelling adults aged 65 and over, replacing the 2015 version and including a clinical reasoning algorithm.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Single-bundle versus double-bundle reconstruction in anterior cruciate ligament: a meta-analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis of 41 RCTs (n=3568) found no significant difference in short/long-term KT-1000/2000 side-to-side differences between single-bundle (SB) and double-bundle (DB) ACL reconstruction. DB showed significantly higher negative pivot-shift test rates (OR=0.62, p<0.001 short-term; OR=0.37, p=0.007 long-term) and higher long-term Lysholm scores (MD=-1.32, p=0.004).
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Approach to sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review of dietary and exercise interventions in the primary care setting
item.description: A systematic review of 6 studies (n=444 in experimental groups) on sarcopenia in older adults found that combined physical exercise and nutritional supplementation in primary care settings demonstrated notable improvements in muscle strength, physical function, and body composition, though results varied with study design and adherence.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: High-impact physical activity participation and 12-month risk of joint replacement: a longitudinal mediation analysis of 17 661 patients with knee or hip osteoarthritis
item.description: A longitudinal mediation analysis (n=17,661) found that high-impact physical activity was associated with 36–48% lower odds of total hip replacement (THR) at 12 months, and was not associated with an altered risk of total knee replacement (TKR) in patients with hip or knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Combining three-dimensional ankle exercises with short-foot training improves proprioception and dynamic balance in female karatekas with flatfoot: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34) found that combining three-dimensional ankle exercises with short-foot training (SF-3DAE) led to greater improvements in navicular drop (2.24 mm vs 1.16 mm), ankle proprioception (3° vs 1.59° error), and dynamic balance (17.49% vs 7.82% Y-Balance total reach) compared to short-foot exercise (SFE) alone in female karate athletes with flatfoot.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Age, resilience, social support, and health literacy as predictors of functional ability in people with spinal cord injury: a 6-month follow-up study.
item.description: A 6-month follow-up study (n=367) on traumatic spinal cord injury patients found that younger age (β=-0.02), higher resilience (β=0.22), and higher health literacy (β=0.32) were significant independent predictors of greater functional ability (Modified Barthel Index) over time, despite only modest overall improvement in MBI scores (from 43.50 to 46.81).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Perceptions and Experiences of Returning to Sport Following Myocardial Infarction: A Qualitative Study.
item.description: A qualitative study explored perceptions of returning to sport post-myocardial infarction, identifying four themes: reconciling active identity with new reality, feeling vulnerable, the need for strong support, and navigating one's own path. Psychosocial challenges, fear, and uncertainty were prominent, highlighting the need for tailored advice and support.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Beliefs and Practices of Pediatric Physiotherapists in Türkiye Regarding Early Mobility and Crawling.
item.description: An online survey of 109 pediatric physiotherapists in Türkiye found that 94.5% believed crawling was important and 63% opposed its removal from CDC developmental checklists. These beliefs influenced therapeutic approaches, with many training hands-and-knees crawling when clinically appropriate.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Prediction model for timing of independent walking on varied surface conditions in patients with early subacute stroke: A multicenter prospective study.
item.description: A multicenter prospective observational study of 168 subacute stroke patients developed and internally validated a Cox proportional hazards model to predict independent walking on varied surfaces, achieving cumulative FAC 5 rate of 51% by week 20, with AUCs from 0.86 to 0.92.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation: a narrative review of clinical applications, proposed mechanisms, and implementation.
item.description: A narrative review synthesizing music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation found consistent evidence for rhythmic auditory stimulation in gait and selected music-supported upper-limb programs, with potential for melodic intonation therapy in nonfluent aphasia, highlighting the need for defined musical ingredients and functional targets.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of adding gait retraining with visual feedback to resistance-balance training on kinematics, centers of pressure, and proprioception in individuals with chronic ankle instability: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that adding gait retraining with visual feedback to resistance-balance training significantly improved proprioception (p=0.001, η²=0.34 for 15° joint position sense), mediolateral center of pressure (p=0.001, η²=0.42), and ankle kinematics in individuals with chronic ankle instability.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil
